problem:
The third-order differential equation ${y}^{‴}-4{y}^{″}+{t}^{2}{y}^{′}+{e}^{t}y=\operatorname{cos}⁡t$ can be expressed as the matrix equation ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+f(t),$ where

| $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,A=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} | {{field-3}} |  | $\,,\,f(t)=\,\,$ |  | {{field-4}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-5}} | {{field-6}} | {{field-7}} |  |  | {{field-8}} |  |  |  |
|  | {{field-9}} | {{field-10}} | {{field-11}} |  |  | {{field-12}} |  |  |  |

and for $y=y(t),$ we have $y={x}_{1}(t),$ ${y}^{′}={x}_{2}(t),$ and ${y}^{″}={x}_{3}(t).$
worked_solution:
We first need to express the given differential equation as a system of first-order differential equations. Then, we write the system as a matrix equation.

We start by making the following change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =y \\ {x}_{2} & ={y}^{′} \\ {x}_{3} & ={y}^{″}\end{aligned}
$$

Differentiating the above equations with respect to $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}={y}^{′}, \\ {x}_{2}^{′}={y}^{″}, \\ {x}_{3}^{′}={y}^{‴}\end{aligned}
$$

which we can rewrite as

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}={x}_{2}, \\ {x}_{2}^{′}={x}_{3}, \\ {x}_{3}^{′}={y}^{‴}.\end{aligned}
$$

We must now write the right-hand side of the last equation in terms of ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},$ and ${x}_{3}.$

Solving our original differential equation for the highest-order derivative $({y}^{‴}),$ we obtain

$$
{y}^{‴}=4{y}^{″}-{t}^{2}{y}^{′}-{e}^{t}y+\operatorname{cos}⁡t.
$$

Then, we substitute our new variables into the right-hand side of the above equation. This gives

$$
{y}^{‴}=4{x}_{3}-{t}^{2}{x}_{2}-{e}^{t}{x}_{1}+\operatorname{cos}⁡t.
$$

Notice that we do not include any derivative terms on the right-hand side. 

Therefore, our complete system of equations is as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}={x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}^{′}={x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}^{′}=-{e}^{t}{x}_{1}-{t}^{2}{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

We can represent this system as the matrix differential equation ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+f(t)$ as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′} \\ {x}_{2}^{′} \\ {x}_{3}^{′}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ -{e}^{t} & -{t}^{2} & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}]
$$
